task_title: Merge train wake-up gaps: always()-dispatch and schedule wake

plan_review.notes: No blocking concerns. Verdict convergent with the two implemented fixes; two non-blocking suggestions (non-CI workflow_run pass-through test, wake-step ordering test) incorporated.
plan_review.summary: Reviewed the two-gap plan: if always on the wake dispatch step; schedule/MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED carve-out mirroring ci-recovery-incidents.yml on the reconcile job guard. Verdict: no blocking concerns, convergent with reviewer own design. Two non-blocking test-coverage suggestions (non-CI workflow_run pass-through, wake-step ordering) were incorporated as new tests.

rounds.summary: No significant issues. Verified YAML precedence/semantics of the schedule carve-out, storm-guard non-regression, safety of if: always() on the wake step (permissions present, desirable behavior when publish job is malformed/cancelled), and correctness of the evaluatesReconcileCondition test-helper substitution approach.

Round 2: reviewed a follow-up delta responding to a copilot-pull-request-reviewer bot finding on an autonomous agent-merge commit -- the retryable-check fallback step reused the original (possibly-failed) app-token output. Added a dedicated recovery-app-token mint step (if: failure()) and rewired the fallback step to use it. Verified if: failure() semantics are job-scoped (fires correctly even if the original app-token mint step is what failed), confirmed graceful degradation if the recovery mint also fails (wake dispatch still fires via if: always() with GITHUB_TOKEN, falling back to the pre-existing staleness bound), confirmed complete test coverage (token reference, step existence/ordering/condition), and found no permission/cost/syntax issues. No significant issues found.

Round 3: reviewed the bounded retry added to the recovery check publication. Verified exactly three attempts, immediate first attempt, 1-second and 2-second waits, early return on success, final-error propagation after exhaustion, and executable parsed-workflow coverage proving third-attempt success. No significant issues found.

Round 4: copilot-pull-request-reviewer flagged that bare `if: failure()` on the recovery-app-token and retryable-check fallback steps also evaluates true when an ANCESTOR job (`verify`, via `needs:`) fails, not just when a step in this job (`publish`) fails. Since `publish` has `if: always()` and `needs: [verify]`, a genuine candidate defect (verify fails) still lets `Publish immutable candidate result` run and correctly post a `failure` conclusion -- but the fallback steps would then fire anyway (ancestor failure(), not this job's own failure) and overwrite that correct `failure` with `cancelled`, causing reconcile to retry a genuinely broken candidate forever instead of bisecting it. Fixed by adding `id: publish` to that step and re-scoping both fallback conditions to `steps.app-token.outcome == 'failure' || steps.publish.outcome == 'failure'` (step-local outcomes, not the job-wide/ancestor-aggregate failure()). Verified via a new semantic test that evaluates the real `if:` expression against simulated step outcomes, proving the ancestor-only-failure case (app-token/publish both success) does not fire while genuine app-token-mint or publish-step failures still do. 3 new regression tests added (24 = 19 + 5 total). No remaining concerns.

Round 5: rather than trust round 4's fix (and GitHub's ambiguous 'any ancestor job' docs phrasing) at face value, ran two real empirical throwaway-workflow probes in nalfeo/Crawler to verify actual runtime semantics. Run 29467076748 (downstream job, if: always(), needs: [upstream] which fails): an implicit-condition step ran and an if: failure() step was skipped -- empirically refuting the original reviewer claim that step-level failure() in an already-running (if: always()) job reflects an ancestor needs: job's failure; it only reflects same-job step outcomes. Cross-checked with a separate-model rubber-duck review (gpt-5.4): verdict AGREE, finding not applicable, no fix needed for that specific concern. Run 29467286711 (bare `if: steps.X.outcome == 'failure'`, no wrapper, X genuinely failed): the step was SKIPPED, proving GitHub Actions implicitly ANDs success() into any if: lacking an explicit status-check function, making round 4's bare-outcome condition self-contradictory dead code -- it could never fire under any circumstance, silently reintroducing the original 40-minute-staleness stall. An independent autonomous agent-merge commit (973e9476) had landed exactly this same dead-code condition while attempting the reviewer's suggested fix, so the regression was real and shipped, not hypothetical. Fixed by changing both fallback conditions to `failure() && (steps.app-token.outcome == 'failure' || steps.publish.outcome == 'failure')` -- the failure() && prefix suppresses the implicit success() AND-ing (making the condition reachable) while the step-local outcome checks remain as defense-in-depth against failure()'s ancestor-job semantics in other job shapes. Updated the explanatory comment block with both run IDs and rationale; updated 3 existing test assertions (2 string checks, 1 semantic eval test now covering 4 cases including a defensive success()-outcome vs failure()-true case) to match; deleted 2 scratch probe workflow files used only for verification. No remaining concerns.

Round 6: reviewed the final recovery-token-success guard layered onto the empirically proven failure() plus step-outcome condition. Verified it remains reachable after original token/publish failure, skips the Checks API call after recovery-mint failure, and preserves genuine candidate failure/bisection behavior. No significant issues found.
